bundle.author: emilybgoodpartyorg
bundle.title: feat(people): a person's own profile photo wins on every card
bundle.body:
On the Garden Grove council position page, Thomas Nguyen appears in a tux (BallotReady's photo, from `assets.civicengine.com`), while his profile shows the photo he uploaded to his GoodParty.org profile (`assets.goodparty.org`). Emily (2026-10-07): the photo the person chose should show wherever they appear.

The profile page already applies that rule (`overlay.avatarUrl ?? person.headshotUrl`); the cards did not. gp-api has no bulk read for profiles, but its `/published` list is a few dozen ids, so a new helper reads that list (cached five minutes), keeps only the card people on it, and fetches those few profiles six at a time. A live profile's avatar then replaces the feed photo on position-page candidates and officeholders, the featured carousel's candidates and officials, and the profile's own related cards. A removed or unpublished profile never yields a photo, and any failure leaves the feed photos in place.

Tests cover the helper (published filter, live only, both failure modes) and one card site each. A doc note records the rule.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Display-only avatar sourcing with safe fallbacks to feed photos; adds bounded gp-api reads for a small published set.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Published GoodParty.org profile photos now override BallotReady feed headshots** on election and profile cards, matching the rule the profile hero already uses.
> 
> A new `resolveProductAvatars` helper loads gp-api’s cached `/published` person-id list, fetches only those people’s live public profiles (six concurrent reads), and returns trimmed `avatarUrl`s. Callers apply the map after building cards in the featured-people carousel, position-page hero candidates and officeholders, and profile “other candidates / nearby officials” lists. **`getPublishedPersonProfileIds`** in `electionsApi` backs the published feed (5-minute revalidate); unreadable lists or profile errors yield an empty map so cards keep feed photos.
> 
> Tests cover the helper (published filter, live-only, failure modes) and one integration path each for featured people and position officeholders. The election redesign doc records the rule.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 0a3de96118647b8ab37d3f08a0ac87f617db7c7f. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

findings.body: **Takedown bypass via product-avatar override.** `buildCandidateCards` / `buildRepresentativeCards` deliberately null the avatar for persons in `removedPersonIds` (via `cardAvatarUrl`), but `withChosenPhoto` unconditionally overwrites `avatarUrl` with the product-avatar URL when `resolveProductAvatars` returns one. `removedPersonIds` comes from election-api's `getRemovedPersonIds`, while `resolveProductAvatars` queries gp-api's `getPublicPersonProfileStatus` — two independent systems with no documented synchronisation guarantee. During any lag (or if the removal workflow reaches election-api before gp-api), a removed person whose gp-api profile is still `'live'` will have their photo reinstated on the featured carousel, violating the invariant stated at `cardAvatarUrl`: "A removed person's photo must not appear anywhere." (Falsification check: `withChosenPhoto` has no access to `removedPersonIds` and performs no guard before applying the override; confirmed by reading lines 343-346.)

**Same takedown bypass in the position-page officeholders loop.** `mapOfficeholderToPerson` sets `avatar: undefined` when the person is in the `removed` set, but lines 176-177 unconditionally overwrite that with the photo from `resolveProductAvatars`. Because `resolveProductAvatars` consults gp-api (independent of election-api's removal list), a removed person with a still-live gp-api profile gets their photo re-applied. (Falsification check: no guard against `removed` exists between `built` and the `chosen` override; the two data sources are fully independent.)

output.summary: This PR adds `resolveProductAvatars`, a helper that fetches live GoodParty.org profile photos and overlays them onto election cards so a person's chosen photo appears everywhere instead of BallotReady's feed photo. The scout flagged five areas; deep-reviewers confirmed a privacy-takedown bypass in two call sites (featuredCandidates.ts and positionOfficeholders.ts) where the new avatar override unconditionally replaces an avatar that was deliberately suppressed for a removed person — the removal list (election-api) and profile status (gp-api) are independent systems with no synchronisation guarantee, so a lag can reinstate a taken-down photo. The same pattern exists in peopleProfile.ts's `withChosenPhotos` but was assessed as lower risk by one reviewer because the gp-api `status === 'live'` check would normally exclude removed profiles; a human reviewer should verify that assumption holds for the election-api removal pathway. The batch-error-drop concern in `productAvatars.ts` was falsified as intentional documented graceful degradation.
